rounds.titleEn: How Do People Take Part in Decisions?
rounds.notes: First BACKLOG-CLEARING round: every new word drawn from the general/breadth decks that had never appeared in any story (290 such words at the time). No fresh vocabulary invented. RESULT: 20/97 = 20.6%. Notably HIGH for a round with no invented vocabulary — confirms these deck words were genuinely unknown, not just unrecorded. Deck presence is not knowledge.

Reinforces ONLY the three STUDIED decks (G, LM, NOPQ) in a new domain. The 52-card abstract deck is NOT yet studied — a round testing it is written and held as story_Z_DEFERRED.txt, to run after that deck is done. RESULT: 19/110 = 17.3%. The three STUDIED decks held almost entirely — راقب، تمويل، إجراء، نفّذ، موقع، دخل، ميزانية، ضخم، منظمة، دولي، دعم، لجنة، مبرر، أبحاث، أجرى، أظهر، مرحلة، اقتصر، امتد، دقة، نسبة، التزم، اختص، مؤرخ، دور، سجّل، حضارة، فشل، كمن all passed. Flags were: (a) genuinely new domain words, and (b) items from the UNSTUDIED abstract deck (القيمة، الجانب، مستقل، ضغط، مؤسسات) — which is expected and confirms the deck-before-reinforcement ordering matters.

Tests the CORRECTED 62-card abstract deck (verbs ماضٍ/مضارع/مصدر، nouns مفرد/جمع، adjectives مذكر/مؤنث). Covers ~38 of 62 deck items — a single story cannot carry all 62 without becoming a word list, so a second story is needed for the remainder (طوّر، نفّذ، تحرر، توقع، شارك، استقر، تعاون، أنجز، انتخب، صوّت، شكا، استحق، استقل، أنفق، زاوية، نوع، مصدر، مواطن، محكمة، قانون، مبلغ، ملحوظ، موثوق، معين). Deck items appear in DIFFERENT paradigm slots than the card face (e.g. card is اِسْتَمَرَّ, story uses الِاسْتِمْرَار) to test whether the 3-slot card transfers across slots.

DELIBERATE FORMAT CORRECTION. Format log showed 17 expository/argumentative rounds vs 1 narrative. This is prose fiction: past-tense narration, no argument, no إن قيل/قلنا، no غير أن. Targets the two gaps his own arabic_deck_v2 flagged as Tier 3 (sensory: light, sound, touch, temperature, smell) and Tier 4 (emotional interiority) — neither had EVER been tested in 27 rounds because expository prose structurally avoids both. RESULT: 6/96 = 6.3% — the LOWEST flag rate of any round so far, and this was an EXPLORE round in a never-tested format. Confirms narrative is genuinely his easiest format (now 2 rounds, both lowest). Sensory vocabulary largely held (بارد، ساخن، صوت، هدوء، نور، أصفر، وجه، صدر، أصابع، يشم، رائحة، شعر، أحس) — the Tier 3/Tier 4 gap his old deck predicted did NOT materialize in reading recognition. Flags were mostly concrete place-nouns (درج، مخبز، حارة) rather than sensory/emotional vocabulary.

Bandit pick: BOTH arms never tried (environment × letter). Letter format brings grammar the article rounds never used — vocative (يا جدي), epistolary opening/closing formulas, sustained 1st-to-2nd person address, and كان + مضارع for habitual past (كنا نجلس، كنت تقول). Topic is drought/climate seen from a personal rather than policy angle, so the environment vocabulary arrives concretely (مطر، بئر، جفّت، مناخ، فصول، خريف، ربيع، ظل، بذور) instead of as abstractions. RESULT: 2/115 = 1.7% — by far the lowest flag rate recorded (previous best was 6.3%). The letter format's distinctive grammar (vocative، epistolary formulas، sustained 2nd-person، كان + مضارع habitual past) caused ZERO flags. Environment vocabulary presented concretely (مطر، بئر، فصول، خريف، ربيع، ظل، بذور، فلاحون، حرّ) also held almost entirely. Suggests personal/epistolary register is very accessible to him — good for volume reading, weak as a diagnostic.

rounds.titleAr: حوار مع باحثة في الذكاء الاصطناعي
rounds.titleEn: An Interview with an AI Researcher
rounds.notes: Bandit pick: both arms never tried (technology × interview). Interview format differs from dialogue — formal س/ج structure, interrogative variety (ما الذي، هل، كيف، ما نصيحتك), and answers in extended expository register rather than conversational turns. Feminine addressee throughout (تصفين، ترددتِ، نصيحتكِ). Drawn words worked in: بتحديد، إدارية، الأقل، نوعا، الاتجاه، المسؤول، تردد، أجراها، بالضبط. RESULT: 18/142 = 12.7%. Pattern in flags: FEMININE 2nd-person verb forms (دَفَعَكِ، تَرَدَّدْتِ، تَصِفِينَ) all flagged despite the underlying verbs being known — a morphological gap, not lexical. Also several already-crammed words reappeared as flags in NEW slots (تَوَقَّعَ as أَتَوَقَّعْ and يَتَوَقَّعُهَا، لَاحَظَ as تُلَاحِظَ، أَجْرَى as أَجْرَاهُ، مَسْؤُول as الْمَسْؤُولَ and الْمَسْؤُولِيَّةَ، اِتِّجَاه، إِدَارِيَّة). Confirms again: knowing a card face does not transfer automatically to other inflections.
